q: Magnetite and Hematite are major ores of which mineral in India?
e: Magnetite (up to 70% iron with magnetic qualities) and Hematite (50–60% iron, most important industrial ore) are the two main types of iron ore.

q: The Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh belt of Jharkhand is the leading producer of which mineral?
e: The Koderma-Gaya-Hazaribagh belt of Jharkhand along the northern edge of Chota Nagpur plateau is the leading producer of mica.

q: Which metal is ultimately obtained from the ore Bauxite?
e: Bauxite is a clay-like ore from which alumina and later aluminium is obtained; Panchpatmali in Koraput (Odisha) is famous for it.

q: Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro in the Damodar valley are major coalfields belonging to which geological age?
e: Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro in the Damodar valley are major Gondwana coalfields, which are over 200 million years old metallurgical coal.

q: Which low-grade brown coal is soft with high moisture content and has principal reserves at Neyveli in Tamil Nadu?
e: Lignite is a low-grade brown coal, soft with high moisture content; principal lignite reserves are in Neyveli in Tamil Nadu.

q: Which is the oldest oil-producing state of India, with Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran-Hugrijan oil fields?
e: Assam is the oldest oil-producing state of India; Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran-Hugrijan are its important oil fields.

q: Balaghat mines (MP), Khetri mines (Rajasthan) and Singhbhum district (Jharkhand) are leading producers of which mineral?
e: The Balaghat mines in MP, Khetri mines in Rajasthan and Singhbhum district of Jharkhand are leading producers of copper.

q: The Monazite sands of Kerala are rich in which atomic energy mineral?
e: The Monazite sands of Kerala are rich in Thorium, used for generating nuclear/atomic power.

q: Which one of the following is a "non-conventional" source of energy?
e: Solar, wind, tidal, geothermal, biogas and atomic energy are non-conventional sources, whereas coal, petroleum, natural gas and firewood are conventional.

q: In which state is India’s largest wind farm cluster located from Nagarcoil to Madurai?
e: The largest wind farm cluster is located in Tamil Nadu from Nagarcoil to Madurai.

q: In which district of Jharkhand are the Gua and Noamundi iron ore mines located?
e: In the Odisha-Jharkhand belt, hematite iron ore is mined in Gua and Noamundi in the Singhbhum district of Jharkhand.

q: Limestone is the basic raw material for which industry?
e: Limestone is the basic raw material for the cement industry and essential for smelting iron ore in the blast furnace.

q: Nearly how many kilograms of manganese are required to manufacture one tonne of steel?
e: Manganese is mainly used in the manufacturing of steel; nearly 10 kg of manganese is required to manufacture one tonne of steel.

q: Parvati valley near Manikaran (Himachal Pradesh) and Puga Valley (Ladakh) are experimental projects for harnessing which energy?
e: Two experimental projects to harness geothermal energy in India are located in the Parvati valley near Manikaran (HP) and the Puga Valley (Ladakh).

q: What is coal mining done by family members in the form of a long narrow tunnel in Jowai and Cherrapunjee (Meghalaya) called?
e: Coal mining in Jowai and Cherrapunjee done by family members in a long narrow tunnel is known as "Rat-hole" mining (declared illegal by NGT).

q: What is the production of goods in large quantities after processing from raw materials to more valuable products called?
e: Production of goods in large quantities after processing from raw materials to more valuable products is called manufacturing.

q: Where was the first successful cotton textile mill established in India in 1854?
e: The first successful textile mill was established in Mumbai in 1854.

q: Where was the first jute mill set up near Kolkata in 1855?
e: The first jute mill was set up near Kolkata in 1855 at Rishra.

q: Which city has emerged as the "electronic capital of India"?
e: Bengaluru has emerged as the electronic capital of India.

q: Which one of the following is an agro-based industry?
e: Cotton, jute, silk, woollen textiles, sugar and edible oil are agro-based industries based on agricultural raw materials.

q: Which one of the following industries uses bauxite as a raw material? [JAC PYQ]
e: Aluminium smelting industry uses bauxite as its raw material.

q: Which one of the following industries manufactures telephones, computers, etc.? [JAC PYQ]
e: Per NCERT textbook exercise, the Electronic industry covers products from transistor sets to telephones, cellular telecom and computers.

q: Which industry is known as the "basic industry" since all heavy, medium and light industries depend on it for their machinery?
e: The iron and steel industry is the basic industry since all other industries—heavy, medium and light—depend on it for their machinery.

q: Which two major integrated iron and steel plants are located in Jharkhand?
e: Jamshedpur (TISCO) and Bokaro Steel Plant are the two major iron and steel plants located in Jharkhand.

q: Where was the first cement plant set up in India in 1904?
e: The first cement plant was set up in Chennai in 1904, and the industry expanded rapidly after Independence.

q: Which of the following is an example of a "joint sector" industry in India?
e: Joint sector industries are jointly run by the state and individuals/group of individuals, such as Oil India Ltd. (OIL).

q: Which plateau region in India has the maximum concentration of iron and steel industries?
e: Chhotanagpur plateau region has the maximum concentration of iron and steel industries due to low cost of iron ore, high grade raw materials in proximity, and cheap labour.

q: Most of India’s jute mills are located in West Bengal mainly along the banks of which river?
e: Most of the jute mills are located in West Bengal, mainly along the banks of the Hugli river, in a narrow belt.

q: Which sectors/examples belong to "cooperative sector" industries in India?
o: Sugar industry in Maharashtra and coir industry in Kerala
e: Cooperative sector industries are owned and operated by producers/suppliers of raw materials or workers, such as the sugar industry in Maharashtra and the coir industry in Kerala.

q: Which energy plant provides twin benefits to farmers in the form of energy and improved quality of manure?
e: Plants using cattle dung ("Gobar gas plants") in rural India provide twin benefits to the farmer in the form of energy and improved quality of manure.

q: Which one of the following minerals is formed by decomposition of rocks, leaving a residual mass of weathered material? [JAC PYQ]
e: Bauxite is formed by the decomposition of surface rocks and the removal of soluble constituents, leaving a residual mass of weathered material containing ores.

q: Which one of the following minerals is contained in the Monazite sand? [JAC PYQ]
e: Thorium is found in abundance in the Monazite sands of Kerala.

q: Koderma, in Jharkhand is the leading producer of which one of the following minerals? [JAC PYQ]
e: Koderma (in the Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh belt of Jharkhand) is the leading producer of mica.

q: Which one of the following agencies markets steel for the public sector plants? [JAC PYQ]
e: All public sector steel undertakings market their steel through Steel Authority of India Ltd. (SAIL).

q: Which iron ore belt in Karnataka contains the Kudremukh 100% export unit sending ore as slurry via pipeline to Mangaluru port?
e: Kudremukh mines in the Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt of Karnataka are a 100% export unit transported as slurry through a pipeline to a port near Mangaluru.

q: Which minerals commonly occur as alluvial "placer deposits" in sands of valley floors and the base of hills?
o: Gold, silver, tin and platinum (not corroded by water)
e: Placer deposits occur as alluvial deposits in sands of valley floors and base of hills, containing minerals not corroded by water: gold, silver, tin and platinum.

q: What does the 1,700 km long Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur (HVJ) cross-country pipeline transport?
e: The 1,700 km long HVJ cross country gas pipeline links Mumbai High and Bassien with fertiliser, power and industrial complexes in western and northern India.

q: In igneous and metamorphic rocks, smaller mineral occurrences in cracks/crevices are called ____ and larger ones are called ____:
e: In igneous and metamorphic rocks, smaller occurrences are called veins and larger ones are called lodes (e.g., tin, copper, zinc and lead).

q: The famous Bailadila hills in Bastar district of Chhattisgarh look like the hump of an ox; what high-grade mineral has 14 deposits there?
o: Super high grade hematite iron ore (exported to Japan and South Korea)
e: Bailadila hills (named after hump of an ox) hold 14 deposits of super high grade hematite iron ore exported to Japan and South Korea via Vishakhapatnam port.

q: Why is mica one of the most indispensable minerals used in electric and electronic industries?
o: Due to its excellent di-electric strength, low power loss factor, insulating properties and resistance to high voltage
e: Due to excellent di-electric strength, low power loss factor, insulating properties and resistance to high voltage, mica is indispensable in electric and electronic industries.

q: In what approximate ratio are iron ore, coking coal and limestone required to make steel?
e: Iron ore, coking coal and limestone are required in the ratio of approximately 4 : 2 : 1 (some quantity of manganese is also required to harden the steel).

q: According to NCERT’s manufacturing process chart, producing 1 tonne of Aluminium requires roughly how much bauxite and alumina?
o: 4 to 6 tonnes of bauxite → 2 tonnes of alumina → 1 tonne of aluminium
e: Per NCERT, 4 to 6 tonnes of bauxite yield 2 tonnes of alumina, which yields 1 tonne of aluminium.

q: Which fertiliser nutrient is entirely imported in India because the country has no reserves of commercially usable potassium compounds?
e: Potash is entirely imported as the country does not have any reserves of commercially usable potash or potassium compounds in any form.

q: NTPC has ISO certification 14001 for which management system?
e: NTPC is a major power providing corporation in India with ISO certification for EMS (Environment Management System) 14001.

q: Which industry is its own largest consumer?
e: The chemical industry is its own largest consumer; basic chemicals undergo processing to further produce other chemicals used for industrial application, agriculture or consumer markets.

q: Which nuclear power station is located near Kota in Rajasthan?
e: Nuclear stations: Tarapur (Maharashtra), Rawatbhata (Rajasthan), Kalpakkam (TN), Narora (UP), Kakrapar (Gujarat) and Kaiga (Karnataka).

q: According to NCERT, how is a small-scale industry defined based on the maximum investment allowed on the assets of a unit?
o: Maximum investment of Rupees one crore
e: A small scale industry is defined with reference to the maximum investment allowed on the assets of a unit; at present the maximum investment allowed is rupees one crore.

q: In which part of India do 55-million-year-old "Tertiary coals" mainly occur?
o: North-eastern states of Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland
e: Tertiary coals (~55 million years old) occur in the north-eastern states of Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

q: Why has there been a tendency for sugar mills to shift and concentrate in southern and western states, especially in Maharashtra?
o: Cane produced here has higher sucrose content, cooler climate ensures a longer crushing season, and cooperatives are more successful here
e: Cane produced in southern/western states (especially Maharashtra) has higher sucrose content, cooler climate ensures a longer crushing season, and cooperatives are more successful.

q: What are "agglomeration economies" in industrial location?
o: Many industries coming together to make use of the advantages offered by urban centres (banking, insurance, transport, labour, consultancy)
e: Cities provide markets and services like banking, insurance, transport, labour and financial advice; many industries tend to come together to benefit from these urban centres, known as agglomeration economies.

q: Petroleum refineries act as a "nodal industry" for which group of industries?
o: Synthetic textile, fertiliser and numerous chemical industries
e: Petroleum refineries act as a "nodal industry" for synthetic textile, fertiliser and numerous chemical industries.

q: Which is the highest quality hard coal?
e: Anthracite is the highest quality hard coal, while Bituminous is the most popular coal in commercial use.

q: Common salt, magnesium and bromine are largely derived from which source?
e: Although ocean waters contain vast quantities of minerals, common salt, magnesium and bromine are largely derived from ocean waters.

q: What dual environmental problem in rural areas is solved when cattle dung is used in Biogas plants instead of burning dung cakes?
o: Prevents loss of trees and manure due to burning fuel wood and cow dung cakes, while giving high-quality fertiliser
e: Biogas has higher thermal efficiency than kerosene, dung cake and charcoal, preventing loss of trees and manure.

q: In India, which regions provide ideal conditions for utilising tidal energy?
o: Gulf of Khambhat, Gulf of Kuchchh (Gujarat) and Gangetic delta in Sunderban regions (West Bengal)
e: In India the Gulf of Khambhat, the Gulf of Kuchchh in Gujarat on the western coast and Gangetic delta in Sunderban regions of West Bengal provide ideal conditions for utilising tidal energy.

q: What is India’s global rank as a producer of raw jute/jute goods and as an exporter (after Bangladesh)?
o: Largest producer of raw jute and jute goods; second largest exporter after Bangladesh
e: India is the largest producer of raw jute and jute goods and stands at second place as an exporter after Bangladesh.

q: What are the two prime factors for the location of the aluminium smelting industry?
o: Regular supply of electricity and an assured source of raw material (bauxite) at minimum cost
e: Regular supply of electricity and an assured source of raw material at minimum cost are the two prime factors for location of aluminium smelting.

q: Which state is India’s largest bauxite producing state, with important Panchpatmali deposits in Koraput district?
e: Odisha is the largest bauxite producing state in India; Panchpatmali deposits in Koraput district are the most important bauxite deposits in the state.

q: Although minerals form a tiny fraction of food intake (about 0.3%), why are they vital for human survival?
o: They are so potent and important that without them we would not be able to utilise the other 99.7% of foodstuffs
e: Although our mineral intake represents only about 0.3 per cent of our total intake of nutrients, they are so potent and important that without them we would not be able to utilise the other 99.7 per cent of foodstuffs.

q: What causes "thermal pollution" of water by industries?
o: When hot water from factories and thermal plants is drained into rivers and ponds before cooling
e: Thermal pollution of water occurs when hot water from factories and thermal plants is drained into rivers and ponds before cooling.

q:
Match the Indian nuclear power station with its state:
A. Kalpakkam — 1. Gujarat
B. Kakrapar — 2. Uttar Pradesh
C. Narora — 3. Tamil Nadu
D. Kaiga — 4. Karnataka
e: Kalpakkam = Tamil Nadu (A-3); Kakrapar = Gujarat (B-1); Narora = UP (C-2); Kaiga = Karnataka (D-4).

q: Why does the textile industry occupy a unique position in the Indian economy?
o: It contributes significantly to industrial production, employment and foreign exchange, and is the only industry in India self-reliant and complete in the value chain
e: It is the only industry in the country which is self-reliant and complete in the value chain i.e., from raw material to the highest value added products.

q: What setback did India’s jute industry suffer due to Partition in 1947?
o: Jute mills remained in India but three-fourth of the jute producing area went to East Pakistan (Bangladesh)
e: After Partition in 1947, the jute mills remained in India but three-fourth of the jute producing area went to Bangladesh (erstwhile East Pakistan).

q: Because the sugar industry is seasonal in nature, it is ideally suited to which ownership sector?
e: The sugar industry is seasonal in nature so it is ideally suited to the cooperative sector.

q: Why was the cotton textile industry concentrated in the cotton growing belt of Maharashtra and Gujarat in its early years?
o: Availability of raw cotton, market, transport including accessible port facilities, labour and moist climate
e: Availability of raw cotton, market, transport including accessible port facilities, labour, moist climate, etc. contributed towards its localisation in Maharashtra and Gujarat.

q: Arrange these major iron and steel plants of India from WEST to EAST:
e: West to East: Bhilai (Chhattisgarh) → Rourkela (Odisha) → Bokaro (Jharkhand) → Durgapur (WB).

q: Which minerals form in sedimentary beds as a result of evaporation, especially in arid regions?
o: Gypsum, potash salt and sodium salt
e: Sedimentary minerals like gypsum, potash salt and sodium salt are formed as a result of evaporation especially in arid regions.

q: Which factor did NOT contribute to the concentration of jute mills along the Hugli river basin?
o: Proximity of jute producing areas and inexpensive water transport
Abundant water for processing raw jute
Cheap labour from WB and adjoining Bihar/Odisha/UP + Kolkata port/banking
Extremely dry desert climate of Thar
e: Thar desert climate played no role; Hugli’s proximity to jute fields, cheap water/rail transport, abundant water, cheap labour and Kolkata banking/port facilities concentrated the mills.

q: Why is conservation of mineral resources urgently required?
o: Geological processes of mineral formation are so slow that rates of replenishment are infinitely small compared to present consumption rates; minerals are finite and non-renewable
Deep mining automatically improves ore grade
e: Workable mineral deposits constitute an insignificant fraction (~1%) of the earth’s crust; formation takes millions of years while consumption is rapid, making them finite and non-renewable.

q: Why does NCERT recommend recycling of metals, using scrap metals and substitutes?
o: To conserve finite mineral resources in a planned and sustainable manner
e: Improved technologies to use low grade ores at low costs, recycling of metals, using scrap metals and other substitutes are key steps in conserving mineral resources.

q: How does the relationship between agriculture and industry show that they "move hand in hand"?
o: Agro-industries boost agricultural productivity by supplying irrigation pumps, fertilisers, insecticides, pipes and machines while sourcing raw materials from agriculture
Agriculture supplies no inputs to factories
e: Agriculture and industry move hand in hand: agro-industries raise agricultural productivity by supplying pumps, fertilisers, pesticides, pipes and tools, while depending on agriculture for raw materials.

q: How is industrial effluent treated across the three phases to prevent water pollution?
o: Primary: mechanical (screening, grinding, flocculation, sedimentation); Secondary: biological; Tertiary: biological, chemical and physical processes including recycling
e: Treatment of industrial effluents is done in three phases: (a) Primary by mechanical means (screening, grinding, flocculation, sedimentation), (b) Secondary by biological process, (c) Tertiary by biological, chemical and physical processes involving recycling.

q: Which devices can be fitted to factory smoke stacks to reduce particulate matter in the air?
o: Electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers and inertial separators
e: Particulate matter in the air can be reduced by fitting smoke stacks to factories with electrostatic precipitators, fabric filters, scrubbers and inertial separators.

q: Why has Aluminium gained popularity as a substitute for steel, copper, zinc and lead in numerous industries?
o: Because it is light, resistant to corrosion, a good conductor of heat, malleable and becomes strong when mixed with other metals
Because it is extremely heavy and brittle
e: Aluminium is light, resistant to corrosion, a good conductor of heat, malleable and becomes strong when mixed with other metals, making it ideal for aircraft, utensils and wires.

q:
Match the energy resource with its primary Indian site:
A. Gondwana Coal — 1. Mumbai High / Digboi
B. Petroleum — 2. Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro
C. Geothermal Energy — 3. Puga Valley (Ladakh) / Manikaran
D. Tidal Energy — 4. Gulf of Kuchchh / Sundarbans
e: Gondwana coal = Jharia/Raniganj/Bokaro (A-2); Petroleum = Mumbai High/Digboi (B-1); Geothermal = Puga Valley/Manikaran (C-3); Tidal = Gulf of Kuchchh/Sundarbans (D-4).

q: Differentiate "Basic/Key industries" from "Consumer industries" using NCERT examples:
o: Basic industries supply products as raw materials to manufacture other goods (iron/steel, copper/aluminium smelting); Consumer industries produce goods for direct use by consumers (sugar, toothpaste, paper, fans)
Steel is consumed raw as food
e: According to their main role: Basic/key industries supply their products as raw materials (iron & steel, copper/aluminium smelting), whereas consumer industries produce goods for direct use by consumers (sugar, toothpaste, paper, sewing machines, fans).

q: Arrange these major iron-ore mining sites from NORTH to SOUTH: 1. Singhbhum (Jharkhand), 2. Bailadila (Chhattisgarh), 3. Kudremukh (Karnataka)
e: Singhbhum (~22°N, Jharkhand) → Bailadila (~18.7°N, Chhattisgarh) → Kudremukh (~13.1°N, Karnataka).

q: According to NCERT’s "Conservation of Energy Resources", what individual citizen actions save energy because "energy saved is energy produced"?
o: Using public transport instead of individual vehicles, switching off electricity when not in use, using power-saving devices and non-conventional energy sources
e: "Energy saved is energy produced": citizens can contribute by using public transport systems, switching off electricity when not in use, using power-saving devices and non-conventional sources.

q: How do geographers and geologists differ in their study of minerals according to NCERT?
o: Geographers study minerals as part of the earth’s crust and their distribution/economic activities, while geologists study formation, age, physical and chemical composition
e: Geographers study minerals as part of earth’s crust, distribution and associated economic activities; geologists study formation, age and physical and chemical composition.

q: Which pair correctly categorises the two main branches of India’s chemical industry (Inorganic vs Organic)?
o: Inorganic: sulphuric acid, nitric acid, alkalies, soda ash, caustic soda; Organic: petrochemicals (synthetic fibres, rubber, plastics, dye-stuffs, drugs & pharmaceuticals)
e: Inorganic chemicals include sulphuric acid, nitric acid, alkalies, soda ash and caustic soda; organic chemicals include petrochemicals used for manufacturing synthetic fibres, rubber, plastics, dye-stuffs, drugs and pharmaceuticals.

q: According to NCERT, what has been the major socio-economic impact of the Information Technology (IT) and Electronics industry in India?
o: A major impact has been on employment generation, with continuing growth in hardware and software being the key to success of IT industry in India
e: A major impact of the electronics/IT industry has been on employment generation; continuing growth in the hardware and software is the key to the success of IT industry in India.

q: Why are inorganic chemical plants widely spread over India, whereas organic chemical plants are located near oil refineries or petrochemical plants?
o: Because organic chemical plants depend on petroleum/petrochemical feedstock near oil refineries, whereas inorganic chemical demand (paper, soap, glass) is spread widely across the country
e: Organic chemical plants are located near oil refineries or petrochemical plants, whereas inorganic chemical industries are widely spread over the country.

q: Which mineral–producing region pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
e: Jharia and Raniganj are major **coal** fields (Damodar valley), not petroleum fields.

q: Which bulky and heavy raw materials are essential for the cement industry alongside coal, electric power and rail transport?
e: Cement requires bulky and heavy raw materials like limestone, silica and gypsum, plus coal, electric power and rail transportation.

q: Coal and some forms of iron ore that have been concentrated as a result of long periods under great heat and pressure occur in beds or layers of which rock type?
e: In sedimentary rocks, minerals like coal and some iron ore occur in beds or layers formed by deposition, accumulation and concentration in horizontal strata under long periods of great heat and pressure.

q: How does industrial and construction noise pollution adversely affect human health?
o: It causes irritation and anger, hearing impairment, increased heart rate and blood pressure among other physiological effects
e: Noise pollution not only results in irritation and anger, it can also cause hearing impairment, increased heart rate and blood pressure.

q: What shared industrial usefulness explains why both Copper and Aluminium are heavily used in electrical transmission/wires?
o: Both are good conductors and malleable/ductile
e: Being malleable, ductile and a good conductor, copper is mainly used in electrical cables; aluminium is similarly light and a good conductor used in wires, utensils and aircraft.

q: Which iron ore belt’s ores, though not of very high quality, are efficiently exploited and exported through Marmagao port?
o: Maharashtra-Goa belt (Goa and Ratnagiri district of Maharashtra)
e: The Maharashtra-Goa belt includes Goa and Ratnagiri district of Maharashtra; though not of very high quality, iron ore is efficiently exploited and exported through Marmagao port.

q: Apart from effluent treatment, what measures should industries take where there is a threat to groundwater reserves?
o: Minimising water use via reuse/recycling, harvesting rainwater to meet water requirements, and legally regulating overdrawing of groundwater reserves
e: NCERT recommends minimising use via reusing/recycling water, rainwater harvesting, and legally regulating overdrawing of groundwater reserves by industry where groundwater is threatened.

q: Which industrial city of Jharkhand is among India’s prominent automobile manufacturing centres listed in NCERT?
e: Automobile manufacturing is located around Delhi, Gurugram, Mumbai, Pune, Chennai, Kolkata, Lucknow, Indore, Hyderabad, Jamshedpur and Bengaluru.

q:
Assertion (A): The Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh belt of Jharkhand is the leading producer of mica.
Reason (R): Mica is indispensable in electric and electronic industries due to its excellent di-electric strength, insulating properties and resistance to high voltage.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true about mica, though mica’s insulating properties do not explain why it occurs in Jharkhand.

q:
Assertion (A): The Chhotanagpur plateau region has the maximum concentration of iron and steel industries in India.
Reason (R): This region offers relative advantages like low cost of iron ore, high grade raw materials in proximity, cheap labour and vast growth potential in the home market.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true and Reason (R) accurately explains why iron and steel industries concentrate in Chhotanagpur plateau.

q:
Assertion (A): "Rat-hole mining" in Jowai and Cherrapunjee (Meghalaya) has been declared illegal by the National Green Tribunal (NGT).
Reason (R): In Meghalaya, coal mining was conducted exclusively by central government mega automated robots rather than local families.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is true, while Reason (R) is false because coal deposits in tribal Meghalaya were mined manually by family members in long narrow tunnels.

q:
Assertion (A): In recent years, there is a tendency for sugar mills to shift and concentrate in southern and western states, especially in Maharashtra.
Reason (R): Sugarcane produced there has higher sucrose content, cooler climate ensures a longer crushing season, and cooperatives are more successful in these states.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are true and Reason (R) explains the shift of sugar mills toward Maharashtra and southern states.

q:
Assertion (A): Conservation of mineral resources is essential for sustainable development.
Reason (R): Geological processes of mineral formation are so slow that the rates of replenishment are infinitely small in comparison to the present rates of consumption.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Slow geological formation versus rapid human consumption explains why finite mineral resources urgently require conservation.

q:
Assertion (A): India exports 100% of its potash fertiliser output because India is the largest global producer of potash minerals.
Reason (R): Actually, India does not have any reserves of commercially usable potash or potassium compounds, so potash is entirely imported.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is true because India entirely imports potash due to lack of domestic reserves.

q:
Assertion (A): Most of the jute mills in India are located in West Bengal along the banks of the Hugli river.
Reason (R): The first cement plant in India was set up in Chennai in 1904.
o: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
e: Both statements are independently true historical/geographical facts, yet the 1904 Chennai cement plant does not explain Hugli’s jute mills.

q:
Assertion (A): Agriculture and industry are not exclusive of each other; they move hand in hand.
Reason (R): Agro-industries depend on agriculture for raw materials and sell products such as irrigation pumps, fertilisers, insecticides, pipes and tools to farmers.

q:
Read the passage: "The growing consumption of energy has resulted in the country becoming increasingly dependent on fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas. Rising prices of oil and gas and their potential shortages have raised uncertainties about the security of energy supply in future, which in turn has serious repercussions on the growth of the national economy. Moreover, increasing use of fossil fuels also causes serious environmental problems. Hence, there is a pressing need to use renewable energy sources like solar energy, wind, tide, biomass and energy from waste material. These are called non-conventional energy sources. India is blessed with an abundance of sunlight, water, wind and biomass."

Why is there a pressing need to shift toward non-conventional energy sources?
o: Rising fossil fuel prices, potential shortages threatening energy security, and serious environmental problems
e: Rising prices, future supply uncertainties due to fossil fuel shortages, and serious environmental problems make renewable non-conventional sources indispensable.

q: Which group listed in the passage represents non-conventional renewable energy sources?
o: Solar, wind, tide, biomass and energy from waste material
e: Solar, wind, tide, biomass and energy from waste material are highlighted as non-conventional renewable energy sources.

q: According to the passage, what four natural endowments is India blessed with in abundance?
o: Only gold, silver, diamond and tin
e: India is blessed with an abundance of sunlight, water, wind and biomass.

q: Which technology directly converts sunlight into electricity?
e: Photovoltaic technology converts sunlight directly into electricity.

q: How does wider adoption of solar/biogas in rural India help conserve forests and farmland?
o: It minimises dependence of rural households on firewood and dung cakes, preserving trees and supplying adequate manure in agriculture
e: Solar plants and biogas reduce reliance on firewood and dung cakes, helping environmental conservation and supplying quality manure.

q:
Read the passage: "Manufacturing industries not only help in modernising agriculture, which forms the backbone of our economy, they also reduce the heavy dependence of people on agricultural income by providing them jobs in secondary and tertiary sectors. Industrial development is a precondition for eradication of unemployment and poverty from our country. This was the main philosophy behind public sector industries and joint sector ventures in India. It was also aimed at bringing down regional disparities by establishing industries in tribal and backward areas. Export of manufactured goods expands trade and commerce, and brings in much needed foreign exchange."

How do manufacturing industries reduce heavy dependence on agricultural income?
o: By providing people jobs in secondary and tertiary sectors
e: Manufacturing reduces heavy dependence on agricultural income by providing jobs in secondary and tertiary sectors.

q: What was the aim of establishing public sector and joint sector industries in tribal and backward areas?
o: Bringing down regional disparities alongside eradicating unemployment and poverty
e: Public/joint ventures in tribal and backward areas aimed at bringing down regional disparities and eradicating poverty and unemployment.

q: According to the passage, what major economic benefit comes from exporting manufactured goods?
o: It expands trade and commerce, and brings in much needed foreign exchange
e: Export of manufactured goods expands trade and commerce and brings in much needed foreign exchange.

q: Countries that transform their raw materials into a wide variety of finished goods of higher value are considered prosperous because:
o: Value-added finished goods yield higher income, broader employment and prosperity than exporting raw materials alone
e: Transforming raw materials into wide varieties of higher-value finished goods creates much greater economic wealth and prosperity.

q: The economic strength of a country is measured by the development of what?
e: The economic strength of a country is measured by the development of manufacturing industries, considered the backbone of development.

q: Which Jharkhand mineral/industrial pair is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Gua and Noamundi (Singhbhum) — Hematite iron ore
Jharia and Bokaro (Damodar valley) — Gondwana coal
Rishra — Located in Jharkhand as a cotton hub
e: Rishra is near Kolkata in West Bengal (site of the first jute mill in 1855), not in Jharkhand. The first three are prime Jharkhand locations.

q:
Consider the following statements about Coal in India:
I. Gondwana coal is over 200 million years old, while Tertiary coal deposits are about 55 million years old.
II. Tertiary coals occur in north-eastern states of Meghalaya, Assam, Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland.
III. Neyveli in Tamil Nadu has the finest grade Anthracite coal reserves.
Which statements are correct?
e: Statements I and II are true. Statement III is false because Neyveli (Tamil Nadu) holds principal reserves of **Lignite** (low-grade brown coal), not Anthracite.

q:
Which practices reflect NTPC’s proactive approach towards preserving the natural environment under ISO 14001?
1. Optimum utilisation of equipment adopting latest techniques and upgrading existing ones
2. Minimising waste generation by maximising ash utilisation
3. Providing green belts for ecological balance and encouraging special purpose vehicles for afforestation
4. Ash pond management, ash water recycling system and liquid waste management
e: All four measures are explicitly documented in NCERT’s NTPC case study for ISO 14001 EMS.

q:
Match the mode of mineral occurrence with its example:
A. Igneous & metamorphic veins/lodes — 1. Alluvial/placer deposits (gold, silver, tin)
B. Sedimentary beds (evaporation) — 2. Bauxite (residual mass)
C. Decomposition of surface rocks — 3. Gypsum, potash salt & sodium salt
D. Valley floor sands — 4. Tin, copper, zinc and lead
e: Veins/lodes = Tin, copper, zinc, lead (A-4); Sedimentary evaporation = Gypsum, potash, sodium salt (B-3); Residual mass = Bauxite (C-2); Placer valley sands = Gold, silver, tin (D-1).

q: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding India’s four major iron-ore belts:
o: Odisha-Jharkhand belt: High grade hematite in Badampahar, Gua & Noamundi
Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur belt: Bailadila hematite exported via Vishakhapatnam to Japan & South Korea
Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru belt: Kudremukh slurry pipeline to Mangaluru port
Maharashtra-Goa belt: Its ore is 100% pure magnetite sent solely by air to Delhi
e: Iron ore from the Maharashtra-Goa belt (though not of highest quality) is efficiently exploited and exported through **Marmagao port**.

q: Identify the INCORRECT mineral–location pair:
o: Bauxite: Amarkantak plateau, Maikal hills, Bilaspur-Katni and Panchpatmali
Mica: Mined exclusively from offshore Mumbai High seabed
e: Mumbai High is an offshore petroleum and natural gas field, not a mica mining zone.

q:
Match the industry ownership sector with its correct example:
1. Public sector — A. Oil India Ltd. (OIL)
2. Private sector — B. BHEL and SAIL
3. Joint sector — C. Sugar industry in Maharashtra
4. Cooperative sector — D. TISCO and Bajaj Auto
e: Public = BHEL/SAIL (1-B); Private = TISCO/Bajaj Auto (2-D); Joint = OIL (3-A); Cooperative = Maharashtra sugar / Kerala coir (4-C).

q: Which set of facts correctly describes Aluminium Smelting in India according to NCERT?
o: It is the second most important metallurgical industry in India; 4–6 tonnes of bauxite yield 2 tonnes alumina then 1 tonne aluminium; used in aircraft, utensils and wires; plants in Odisha, WB, Kerala, UP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and TN
e: All details match NCERT’s description of India’s second most important metallurgical industry (after iron & steel).

q: What shared geographical factor made Jharkhand home to both India’s early private steel pioneer (Jamshedpur) and public sector Bokaro Steel Plant?
o: Exceptional proximity on the Chhotanagpur plateau to Singhbhum/Odisha iron ore, Damodar valley coking coal (Jharia-Bokaro), limestone, river water and cheap labour
e: Chhotanagpur plateau’s unique co-location of high-grade iron ore, coking coal, limestone, water and cheap labour anchored Jamshedpur and Bokaro.

q: In India, in which geological rock structures do petroleum occurrences mostly occur?
o: In anticlines and fault traps in rock formations of the tertiary age, trapped within porous limestone/sandstone between non-porous layers
e: Most petroleum occurrences in India are associated with anticlines and fault traps in tertiary rock formations; porous strata hold oil/gas sealed by non-porous layers, with lighter gas above oil.

q: Match the three major agro-based industries with their prominent state concentrations:
o: Cotton: Maharashtra & Gujarat; Jute: West Bengal (Hugli); Sugar: UP, Bihar & Maharashtra
Cotton: Assam; Jute: Rajasthan; Sugar: Ladakh
e: Cotton textiles concentrate in Maharashtra/Gujarat/TN; Jute along Hugli in WB; Sugar mills in UP, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka and TN.

q: How does cotton Spinning differ structurally from cotton Weaving in India as highlighted in NCERT?
o: Spinning continues to be centralised in Maharashtra, Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, while weaving is highly decentralised to incorporate traditional skills and designs in cotton, silk, zari and embroidery
Weaving occurs in just one plant
e: Spinning is centralised in Maharashtra, Gujarat and TN, whereas weaving is highly decentralised to incorporate traditional regional skills and designs.

q: Which industries discharge dangerous organic and inorganic wastes like dyes, detergents, acids, salts, lead and mercury into rivers?
o: Paper, pulp, chemical, textile and dyeing, petroleum refineries, tanneries and electroplating industries
e: Main culprits of industrial water pollution are paper, pulp, chemical, textile/dyeing, refineries, tanneries and electroplating discharging dyes, detergents, acids, salts, lead and mercury.

q: Fly ash, phospo-gypsum and iron and steel slags are listed in NCERT primarily as major solid wastes polluting which medium?
o: Major solid wastes polluting water and land in India
e: Fly ash, phospo-gypsum and iron and steel slags are major solid wastes in India affecting water and soil.

q: Which statement regarding Energy Resources in India is INCORRECT?
o: Conventional sources include firewood, cattle dung cake, coal, petroleum, natural gas and electricity
Firewood and cattle dung cake meet >70% of energy requirement in rural households
Coal occurs in forms of peat, lignite, bituminous and anthracite
Nuclear power exists only in Rajasthan as no other state has atomic plants
e: India has operational nuclear stations across six states: Maharashtra, Rajasthan, TN, UP, Gujarat and Karnataka.

q: Vishakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Marmagao ports share a vital role in exporting which Indian mineral?
e: Bailadila ore exports via Vishakhapatnam, Kudremukh via Mangaluru, and Goa-Ratnagiri via Marmagao port.

q: Which grade of coal and Indian basin is most valuable as metallurgical coal for smelting iron in blast furnaces?
o: High grade bituminous coal (metallurgical Gondwana coal) — Damodar valley (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro)
e: High grade bituminous coal is metallurgical coal with special value for smelting iron in blast furnaces; Gondwana deposits lie in Jharia, Raniganj and Bokaro.

q: Match "Heavy" vs "Light" industries based on the bulk and weight of raw materials and finished goods:
o: Heavy industry: Iron and steel; Light industry: Electrical goods industries (using light raw materials and producing light goods)
Heavy: sewing machines; Light: Iron & cement
e: Based on bulk and weight of raw material and finished goods: Heavy industries use heavy materials like iron & steel, whereas light industries use light raw materials to produce light goods such as electrical goods industries.

q: How does replacing coal with oil or gas in factories, alongside fitting silencers to generators, mitigate dual industrial hazards?
o: Using oil or gas instead of coal reduces smoke/air pollution, while fitting silencers and noise-absorbing materials reduces noise pollution
e: Smoke can be reduced by using oil or gas instead of coal in factories, and generators should be fitted with silencers alongside noise-absorbing materials to cut noise pollution.

q:
Arrange the establishment of India’s first modern mills/plants in these three industries chronologically:
1. First cement plant in Chennai
2. First successful cotton textile mill in Mumbai
3. First jute mill at Rishra near Kolkata
e: Mumbai cotton mill (1854) → Rishra jute mill (1855) → Chennai cement plant (1904).

q: Besides Jharkhand’s Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh belt, which two states contain the major mica producing belts of Ajmer and Nellore?
e: In Rajasthan, the major mica producing area is around Ajmer; Nellore mica belt is in Andhra Pradesh.

q: Ferrous minerals account for about three-fourths of the total value of metallic mineral production in India. Which pair consists exclusively of FERROUS minerals?
e: Ferrous minerals (iron ore, manganese, nickel, cobalt) account for about three-fourths of total metallic mineral production value, providing a strong base for metallurgical industries; copper and bauxite are non-ferrous.

q: Which statement about Indian mineral/steel hubs is INCORRECT?
o: Khetri copper mines are in Rajasthan
Balaghat copper mines are in Madhya Pradesh
Panchpatmali bauxite deposits are in Koraput district, Odisha
Bhilai and Visakhapatnam steel plants are in Punjab and Haryana
e: Bhilai is in Chhattisgarh and Visakhapatnam is in Andhra Pradesh—not Punjab or Haryana.

q: When does a mineral "deposit" or "reserve" actually turn into a "mine"?
o: When concentration of mineral in ore, ease of extraction and closeness to market make extraction economically viable
When it lies 100 km deep in trace amounts
e: Concentration of mineral in the ore, ease of extraction and closeness to market affect the economic viability of a reserve; when this choice is met, a deposit turns into a mine.

q: Spot the INCORRECT fact about Petroleum and Natural Gas in India:
o: Ankeleshwar is the most important oil field of Gujarat
Digboi, Naharkatiya and Moran-Hugrijan are important oil fields in Assam
Mumbai High is a major offshore petroleum field off the western coast
The HVJ pipeline runs exclusively inside the state of Kerala
e: The 1,700 km HVJ (Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur) pipeline links Mumbai High/Bassien across Gujarat, MP and UP to industrial hubs in western & northern India, not inside Kerala.

q: Why do Gujarat-based cement plants enjoy strategic export advantages, and how does Gujarat perform in fertilisers?
o: Cement plants in Gujarat have suitable access to the market in Gulf countries, and Gujarat is also a major fertiliser producer alongside TN, UP, Punjab and Kerala
e: Cement plants in Gujarat access Gulf markets easily; Gujarat, TN, UP, Punjab and Kerala contribute towards half of India’s fertiliser production.

q: Which structural weakness in India’s cotton textile sector is noted in NCERT despite world-class spinning capacity?
o: Although spinning produces good quality yarn at global standards, weaving, knitting and processing units cannot use much of the high-quality yarn produced in the country due to fragmented small units
e: India has world-class spinning production, but weaving supplies low quality fabric as it cannot use much of the high quality yarn produced in the country (fragmented small units).

q: In which non-conventional energy sector is India emerging as a global superpower as highlighted in NCERT? [JAC Model]
e: India has great potential of wind power (Tamil Nadu Nagarcoil–Madurai, AP, Karnataka, Gujarat, Kerala, Maharashtra, Lakshadweep, Jaisalmer).

q: Arrange the four varieties of coal in ASCENDING order of quality and carbon content (lowest to highest):
e: Ascending quality order: Peat (low carbon, high moisture) → Lignite (low-grade brown coal) → Bituminous (commercial/metallurgical) → Anthracite (highest quality hard coal).

q: Among complex geographical and human factors, what single economic principle governs the key decision of industrial factory location?
o: Least cost of production—finding locations where raw materials, labour, capital, power and market are available at the lowest combined cost
e: Industrial locations are complex; naturally, manufacturing activity tends to locate at the most appropriate place where all factors of industrial location are either available or can be arranged at lower cost.
